verdict: Tesla closed 2024 with record deliveries and record revenue of $25.7B, but price cuts squeezed car profits — operating income fell 23% to $1.6B, and only booming energy and services revenue kept total revenue growing.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $2.27 a year ago — that quarter carried a one-time tax benefit

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: operating cash flow of $4.8B, capex of $2.8B

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Selling and leasing cars, plus $692M of regulatory credits — revenue fell 8% as average prices came down, even though deliveries hit a record 495,570.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack batteries and solar — storage deployments hit a record 11.0 GWh, up 244% YoY, and revenue more than doubled.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, repairs, insurance and used-car sales — up 31%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI, the Optimus robot, Cybercab and new vehicles.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: One-off costs of reshaping the business — just $7M this quarter, after much bigger charges earlier in 2024.

otherDetail: Interest income of $442M, plus $837M of other income — largely fair-value gains on Tesla's bitcoin holdings and currency gains — less $96M of interest expense: a net +$1,183M below operating profit.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $2,332M; $2,317M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).

takeaways.title: A record quarter for deliveries
takeaways.text: Tesla delivered a record 495,570 vehicles and deployed a record 11.0 GWh of energy storage — but it cut prices to get there, so automotive revenue still fell 8% YoY.

takeaways.title: Energy is the growth story
takeaways.text: Energy generation and storage revenue more than doubled to $3.1B and services grew 31% — together they added about $1.8B of revenue versus a year ago and kept total revenue growing.

takeaways.title: A bitcoin gain flattered the bottom line
takeaways.text: Other income swung from a $270M expense in Q3 to +$837M, helped by fair-value gains on Tesla's bitcoin holdings. And GAAP EPS of $0.66 only looks weak next to Q4 2023's $2.27 because that quarter included a one-time $5.8B tax benefit.

oneTimers: Bitcoin remeasurement: Tesla's other income includes fair-value gains on its bitcoin holdings after new crypto accounting rules took effect on January 1, 2024 — the 10-K records a $589M unrealized gain on digital assets for 2024 as a whole.

The year-ago comparison is distorted: Q4 2023 net income was boosted by a one-time $5,752M tax benefit (release of a valuation allowance), which is why GAAP net income shows a 71% YoY drop even though operations were steadier.
